verdict.rationale: Datalab's own docs say the conversion API (Marker) parses PDFs into Markdown, HTML, or JSON and 'handles complex layouts, tables, math, and images'. Hands-on community reports are mixed: one user found it does a 'reasonable job' but intermingled columns in tricky cases, and another found tables and text boxes messed up on an RPG rulebook. Those reports concern the open-source Marker and are not clear enough failures to make the claim disputed. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of header/footer/footnote handling and reading-order guarantees, multi-column-specific accuracy evidence, and independent corroboration of clean ordering on complex layouts.

support.subject: As a developer, the API parses complex real-world PDFs — multi-column layouts, headers, footers, footnotes — into clean, correctly ordered content

citations.quote: Marker handles complex layouts, tables, math, and images.
